KB_START.text: Main Menu: Please choose your symptom type

BRANCH_A.text: Branch A: Choose the description that best fits your condition

options.label: Red patches, painful joints, pitted nails, or dandruff
Blackheads/whiteheads, oily skin, pimples or cysts

A_PSORIASIS_CHECK.text: Detailed Check: Do the patches develop white-silvery scales and stiffness?

options.label: No, it's more of oozing blisters

BRANCH_B.text: Branch B: Choose the symptoms you are experiencing with fever

options.label: Severe headache, stiff neck, and confusion
Cough, runny nose, and spreading itchy rash

MENINGITIS_CHECK.text: Urgent Check: Do you have a stiff neck along with the headache and rash?

MEASLES_SCARLET_CHECK.text: Infection Check: Do you have grayish bumps in the mouth (Koplik spots)?

options.label: Red, painful lump following an insect bite
Firm round lumps with rough surface and black dots

Acne.text: Is your skin notably oily, especially in the T-zone (forehead, nose, and chin)?
Do you have deep, painful lumps or cysts under the skin that do not come to a head?
Do you frequently get red or swollen pimples that may be painful or last several days?

Psoriasis.text: Do you notice silvery-white scales on the red, raised patches of skin?
Do you experience any stiffness, swelling, or pain in your joints?
Are there any pits, thickening, or discoloration in your fingernails or toenails?

Eczema.text: Is the itching intense, particularly at night or after contact with certain fabrics or soaps?
Do the affected areas ooze fluid or crust over, especially when scratched?
Does the skin feel thick or leathery (lichenified) in areas that are frequently scratched?

Melanoma.text: If you draw an imaginary line through the spot, do the two halves look noticeably different from each other?
Does the spot contain multiple shades of color — such as tan, brown, black, red, white, or blue — within the same lesion?
Has the spot changed in size, shape, color, or started to bleed, itch, or crust over in recent weeks or months?

Basal Cell Carcinoma.text: Does the growth appear pearly, shiny, or translucent, sometimes with small visible blood vessels on its surface?
Has the sore or lesion failed to fully heal, or does it repeatedly bleed or crust over and then reopen?
Is the lesion located on an area that has had significant sun exposure, such as the face, ears, neck, or scalp?

Benign Keratosis-like Lesions.text: Does the growth look or feel as if it has been stuck or pasted onto the skin rather than growing from within it?
Is the surface of the lesion waxy, scaly, or rough, and is it tan, brown, or black in color?
Did this growth appear gradually during middle age or later, and have you noticed more of them over time?

Seborrheic Keratoses.text: Does the lesion have a distinctive 'stuck-on' appearance, as if it could be peeled off the skin?
Is the lesion light tan, brown, or black with a waxy or greasy surface texture?
Do you have multiple similar growths appearing on your back, chest, face, or scalp?

Warts Molluscum.text: Is the surface of the bump rough, grainy, or cauliflower-like to the touch, or alternatively smooth and dome-shaped with a small dimple in the center?
Can you see tiny black dots inside the lesion, or does it have a small central indent or pit (umbilication)?
Have similar bumps appeared in clusters or spread to nearby skin areas, or to others who share close physical contact with you?

Tinea Ringworm Candidiasis.text: Does the rash form a ring or circular shape with a raised, scaly, or redder outer edge and a clearer center?
Is the rash located in a warm, moist area of the body such as the groin, underarms, between toes, or skin folds?
Have you recently had contact with animals, soil, shared locker rooms or pools, or someone with a similar rash?

Melanocytic Nevi.text: Has this mole been present for a long time and remained essentially the same in size, shape, and color?
Is the mole's color evenly distributed (uniform brown or tan) and does it have a smooth, well-defined border?
Is the mole free of symptoms such as itching, bleeding, crusting, or pain?
